To kill a Python process on Linux from the command line, you can use the `pkill` command followed by the name of the Python executable, like this:

```bash
pkill -f python
```

This command will send a SIGTERM signal to all processes matching "python". If the process doesn't terminate, you can use the `-9` option to send a SIGKILL signal, which forcefully kills the process:

```bash
pkill -9 -f python
```

Alternatively, you can use `kill` with the process ID (PID) if you know it:

```bash
kill -9 <PID>
```

Replace `<PID>` with the actual process ID of the Python process you want to terminate.
